chunks.title: KfW Development Bank (Germany) (KfW) COP31 Role & Commitments
chunks.text: KfW Development Bank (Germany) is a Bilateral DFI headquartered in Germany. At UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya (November 9-20, 2026), its verified role is: Executive Board delegation at COP31; signed €250M green transition loan with Turk Eximbank; climate mobility & energy panels. Verified COP31 2026 climate finance commitment: €250M COP31 loan with Turk Eximbank + €415B cumulative climate & environmental commitments since 2017. Source verification: https://www.kfw.de/About-KfW/Newsroom/Latest-News/S12-Themenseite-3.html.

chunks.title: KfW Financing Instruments & Ticket Bounds
chunks.text: KfW Development Bank (Germany) provides the following climate financing instruments: Promotional Loan, Concessional Development Loan, Grant (IKI / BMZ), Green Credit Line, Climate Venture Capital. Typical transaction ticket range is USD 5,000,000 to USD 350,000,000. Eligible applicant profiles include: Sovereign/Government, Financial Intermediary, Municipality, Large Corporate, Project SPV.

chunks.title: KfW Priority Climate Sectors & Regional Mandate
chunks.text: Priority climate sectors funded by KfW Development Bank (Germany): Renewable Energy, Urban Mobility & Transport, Energy Efficiency & Green Buildings, Biodiversity & Nature, Industrial Decarbonization, Climate Adaptation & Resilience. Target geographic focus includes: Global, Germany, Europe, Türkiye, Emerging Markets, Developing Countries, Africa, Asia. Projects outside primary regions or ticket bounds may require syndicated or on-lending structures.

chunks.title: KfW Mandatory Form & Underwriting Requirements
chunks.text: Mandatory requirements to complete KfW's application form: KfW Sustainability Guideline & Environmental/Social Impact Assessment; Paris Agreement compatibility & GHG accounting; Partner-country government or bank intermediary mandate; IFC Performance Standards / EU environmental benchmark. Explicit exclusion rules: Coal power/mining; Unabated fossil fuel expansion. Official application portal: https://www.kfw-entwicklungsbank.de/.

chunks.title: KfW Form Template: Development Finance Institution (DFI) / National Dev Bank Project Intake Form
chunks.text: KfW Development Bank (Germany) uses the 'Development Finance Institution (DFI) / National Dev Bank Project Intake Form' workflow governed by IFC Performance Standards / Harmonized DFI Climate Reporting (10by30 / IDFC). Typical review timeline is 4–12 weeks (Screening -> Due Diligence -> Credit Committee). Form sections required: 1. Sponsor Profile, 2. Transaction Structure, 3. Climate & Impact, 4. Financial Due Diligence, 5. Risk Assessment, 6. Executive Summary.
